  • A: Cryopreservation is the preservation of living cells and tissues in liquid nitrogen (LN) at − 196 °C

questions.question: Explain the significance of protoplast fusion in the creation of somatic hybrids and cybrids. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of protoplast fusion in the creation of somatic hybrids and cybrids.
  • A: Protoplast fusion is the biotechnological process involving the aseptic mixing up of protoplasts
  • from two different plants. This process is used to create new varieties with desirable traits, such as
  • disease resistance, by either combining the entire genomes to form a somatic hybrid or fusing nuclei
  • from one parent with cytoplasm from both to create a cybrid. It is helpful in overcoming sexual
  • barriers, crop improvement and overcoming sexual barriers, crop improvement, genetic research,
  • novel plant varieties and cytoplasmic inheritance. (any three valid points )

questions.question: Discuss the techniques and significance of somatic hybridization and cybridization. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the techniques and significance of somatic hybridization and cybridization.
  • A: Somatic hybridization and cybridization are biotechnological techniques that enable the
  • combination of genetic material from different plant species, overcoming barriers of sexual
  • incompatibility.
  • Somatic Hybridization
  • This method fuses protoplasts—plant cells without cell walls—from two species to form a hybrid
  • containing both nuclear and cytoplasmic genomes.
  • Technique: Protoplasts are first isolated by enzymatically removing cell walls using cellulase and
  • pectinase. The protoplasts are then cultured in a nutrient medium and fused using chemical agents like
  • polyethylene glycol (PEG) or electrical pulses. Hybrid cells are selected through metabolic markers or
  • fluorescence and regenerated into whole plants.
  • Significance: Somatic hybridization enables the creation of novel genetic combinations which are not
  • possible through sexual crosses, including interspecific or intergeneric hybrids. It can produce fertile
  • plants from sterile parents and introduce valuable cytoplasmic traits like disease resistance or stress
  • tolerance. Applications include developing disease-resistant Citrus varieties and improving fruit
  • quality in persimmons.
  • Cybridization
  • Cybridization, or cytoplasmic hybridization, involves the fusion of a whole protoplast from one parent
  • with an enucleated protoplast (cytoplast) from another. The resulting cybrid carries the nuclear
  • genome of one species and the cytoplasm of both.
  • Technique: One parent’s cells are enucleated, and these cytoplasts are fused with intact donor
  • protoplasts. The resulting cells are cultured and regenerated into plants.
  • Significance: Cybridization allows selective transfer of cytoplasmic traits—such as cytoplasmic male
  • sterility, herbicide tolerance, or disease resistance—without altering the nuclear genome. It is
  • particularly useful in breeding programs to introduce desirable cytoplasmic characteristics while
  • retaining the superior nuclear background of a cultivar.

questions.question: What is organic farming? Discuss the benefits and challenges of organic farming. / [CO5] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• What is organic farming? Discuss the benefits and challenges of organic farming.
  • A: Organic farming is a sustainable agricultural system that avoids synthetic inputs like pesticides,
  • fertilizers, and GMOs, and instead emphasizes natural processes and materials to build soil health and
  • fertility.
  • Benefits of Organic Farming:
  • • Economical Farming
  • • Environment Friendly
  • • Sustains Soil Fertility
  • • Provides Healthy Food
  • • Inexpensive technique
  • • Generates Income through Exports
  • Challenges before Organic Farming
  • • Less Popular
  • • Lack of Infrastructure and Marketing Facilities
  • • Low Yield
  • • Shorter Food Life
  • • Limited Choice of Crops
  • (Definition 2marks + Benefits 4 marks + Challenge 4marks)
